subject: Renewal path and technical credit for Q4 surge
messages:

Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity top-up + co-term question for Q4

Hi Lauren,

Quick note — Novex is seeing an expected 20–30% surge in inference volume starting in October tied to a pilot rollout. We’re mid-way through our annual contract with Redwood and want to explore options for adding capacity without waiting for the renewal window.

Specifically, procurement asked for:
- A short-term top-up (targeting +25% capacity) that can be co-termed at renewal;
- Pricing options (pro-rata vs voucher vs temporary credit);
- Any one-time onboarding or infra credits you can offer to help with cost predictability;
- Confirmation of how caching/batching behaviour will impact unit price; and
- Timeline and docs procurement needs (SOW amendment, PO, security checklist).

Can you share 2–3 concrete paths and rough numbers? Our preferred timeline is to have something signed by mid‑July so the Oct rollout is covered.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Carter
Procurement Lead, Novex Health
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@novexhealth.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@novexhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity top-up + co-term question for Q4

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask. I pulled the May usage report (attached) and sketched three practical paths below; I also linked the HubSpot record for reference.

(Attachment: usage-report-may.csv)

Options — quick summary with estimated impact (ballpark):
1) Pro‑rata top-up (one-time add until contract renewal)
   - +25% committed units, pro‑rated for remaining term (effective immediately)
   - No long-term discount; unit price = current rate; estimated monthly delta: ~$18k
   - Fastest path for procurement — PO + amendment (2 weeks)

2) Voucher / prepaid cushion (short-term voucher bucket)
   - Buy a 3‑month voucher at 95% of list for the extra capacity; unused vignette rolls into renewal credit
   - ~5% uplift discount for prepaid commit; good if you want predictability

3) Temporary technical credit + co-term annualize (preferred for growth)
   - Apply a one-time onboarding/technical credit (covers part of top-up) and commit to annualize the extra capacity at renewal for a 10% blended discount on the new baseline
   - Requires amendment + co‑term election at renewal (legal review)

My recommendation: option 3 balances cost and long-term predictability. I can put firm numbers together once we confirm whether Novex wants a temporary 3‑month cushion or to commit to annualizing the increase.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm preferred path by Friday 6/13
- I’ll loop in Ben (pricing lead) and Kimberly (legal) to draft the amendment and a short SOW addendum
- Target DocuSign by 7/10, effective 7/15 so billing aligns for July usage

Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/engagements/NX-2025-511

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity top-up + co-term question for Q4

Lauren / Kimberly — quick internal:

I ran margin sims on the three options Lauren outlined. High level recommendations:
- If Novex wants to avoid long-term commitment, go with option 2 (voucher) — we can offer a 5% prepaid discount. Low operational lift, preserves renewal dynamics.
- If they will annualize the uplift at renewal (option 3), we can support a 10% blended discount on the new baseline but need: clear commit period, updated SLOs in the SOW for the higher baseline, and a short SLA carveout for burst capacity.

Risks/caveats:
- Anything that moves pricing below 10% discount on committed units will materially widen our margin delta for their usage profile; we should avoid open-ended credits.
- Legal: Kimberly, please prepare a 1‑page amendment template that includes: amended baseline units, effective date, billing pro‑rata rule, and an SLA note about burst rebalancing. Also include standard data retention and audit language.

I’ll draft the pricing table once Kimberly confirms the amendment language.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Emily / Raj — following up with a concrete proposal and next steps. Per our internal review we can support an \"accelerated renewal path\" with a technical credit. Please find attached the SOW addendum (Novex-SOW-v2.pdf) and the May usage snapshot.

Proposal (summary):
- Effective date: 2025-07-15
- Temporary top-up: +25% baseline units through renewal (applies immediately)
- Technical credit: one-time credit equal to 40% of the first-month uplift to offset onboarding and burst costs (applied to July invoice)
- Annualize option at renewal: If Novex elects to annualize the +25% at renewal, we’ll apply a 10% blended discount on the new baseline for the first 12 months post-renewal
- Billing: pro‑rata for July; thereafter billed monthly per amended baseline
- Payment terms: Net 30

Docs and next steps:
1) Review SOW addendum (attached Novex-SOW-v2.pdf) — this includes the updated baseline, SLA carveout, and billing pro‑rata clause.
2) If approved, sign via DocuSign link (we’ll send the envelope) and issue a PO referencing NX-2025-511.
3) Once signed, we’ll spin up the capacity change the following Monday and confirm KV cache warming schedule with your infra lead.

If this looks good I’ll send the DocuSign and the pricing table Ben mentioned. Happy to hop on a 30‑minute call if you want to run numbers together this week.
